what_its_for: Arformoterol is a long-acting bronchodilator (airway opener) used to treat chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), including chronic bronchitis and emphysema. It helps relax and open up the airways in your lungs so you can breathe more easily. It is used as a maintenance (regular, long-term) treatment and is NOT meant to treat sudden breathing attacks or shortness of breath.
how_to_take: Arformoterol comes as a liquid solution used with a nebulizer machine. Open one single-use vial and pour the entire contents into your nebulizer cup. Attach the mouthpiece or face mask and breathe in the mist slowly and deeply until all the medication is gone (usually about 5 to 15 minutes). Never swallow this medication. Never mix it with other nebulizer medicines unless your doctor or pharmacist says it is okay. Rinse your nebulizer equipment after each use according to the manufacturer's instructions.
dosing: The usual adult dose is one 15 mcg vial (2 mL) inhaled through a nebulizer twice a day — once in the morning and once in the evening, about 12 hours apart. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions. Do not use more than 2 vials (one in the morning and one in the evening) in a single day.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regularly scheduled time. Do not double up or take an extra dose to make up for the one you missed. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store unopened vials in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep the vials in their foil pouch until you are ready to use them to protect them from light. If you need to store them at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C), use them within 6 weeks. Do not freeze. Throw away any open, unused vials right away. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Do not use arformoterol as a rescue inhaler for sudden breathing problems — always have a fast-acting rescue inhaler (like albuterol) available for emergencies. Avoid using other long-acting bronchodilators (such as salmeterol or formoterol) at the same time unless your doctor approves. Let your doctor know about all medications you take, especially beta-blockers (used for heart problems or blood pressure), certain antidepressants (MAOIs or tricyclics), and diuretics (water pills), as these can interact with arformoterol. Avoid smoking, as it worsens COPD.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: sudden wheezing or worsening shortness of breath after using this medication, chest pain or tightness, fast or pounding heartbeat, high blood pressure, tremors or shaking, low potassium symptoms (muscle cramps or weakness), signs of a serious allergic reaction (rash, hives, swelling of face, lips, or throat, difficulty swallowing or breathing), or if your rescue inhaler is not working as well as usual. Also call your doctor if your breathing problems do not improve or get worse over time.
when_it_works: Arformoterol starts to work within 7 to 20 minutes after inhaling it, but it is meant for long-term maintenance use — not for immediate relief. You should use it every day as prescribed, even when you feel well, to keep your airways open and prevent breathing problems. It may take a few weeks of regular use to notice the full benefits.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): This medication can be used in older adults, but they may be more sensitive to side effects such as rapid heartbeat and tremors. Monitor closely. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of arformoterol during pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been fully established. Children: Arformoterol is not approved for use in children or adolescents under 18 years of age. Kidney or liver problems: If you have liver or kidney disease, talk to your doctor, as dose adjustments may be needed.
